_comment: Canonical tier → provider model id map. To add a new provider, add a column to each tier entry (and an effort entry if applicable). Source agents/commands only declare their tier; the renderer looks the model id up here.
_claude_note: The `claude` column holds Claude Code model ALIASES (opus/sonnet/haiku), not pinned model ids. Claude Code resolves an alias to the current model of that family, so the column never goes stale on a model launch — pinned ids did, which is why they were replaced. This value is mirrored into each agent's `model:` frontmatter key and into its run-banner row; helpers/agent-lint.sh fails on any drift between the three.
_claude_resolves_to: As of 2026-07-31: opus → Claude Opus 5 ($5/$25 per MTok) · sonnet → Claude Sonnet 5 ($3/$15, introductory $2/$10 through 2026-08-31) · haiku → Claude Haiku 4.5 ($1/$5, 200K context vs 1M on the others).

reasoning._roles: architecture, planning, refactoring, security analysis, onboarding decisions

backend-exec._roles: backend implementation, backend review, code review, database, devops, qa, mobile, backend tests

frontend._roles: frontend implementation, frontend review, frontend tests, ui/ux design

repetitive._roles: doc generation, changelogs, release notes, boilerplate, high-volume low-judgment tasks

effort._comment: Per-tier per-provider effort/variant value injected into the provider's native effort field. An omitted provider key means that tier does not set effort for that provider.
effort._claude_note: Claude Code DOES support a per-subagent `effort:` frontmatter key (low/medium/high/xhigh/max) — an earlier revision of this file wrongly claimed it had no effort concept. It is set deliberately for `repetitive` only: that tier is bounded, low-judgment work where `low` is a clear win. The other tiers omit it on purpose, because the key OVERRIDES the session's effort level — setting it everywhere would silently undo a user who lowered effort for cost or latency. Omitted = inherits the session, which is the right default.

agent_effort._comment: Per-agent effort override, keyed by agent name then provider. Takes precedence over the tier-level `effort` map above. Exists because effort tracks how much a role needs to REASON, which does not always follow the tier that picks its model — the five agents below run on Sonnet or write to spec, but the work itself is directed enough that the extra exploration does not pay for itself.
agent_effort._why_not_security_specialist: security-specialist is deliberately absent. Low effort means fewer, more consolidated tool calls and less exploration before answering — in a security audit that exploration is the product, and cutting it is how a vulnerability goes unreported. Do not add it here without a specific reason.
